source: If the agent had chosen otherwise, the outcome would have changed. The outcome did not change. Therefore the agent did not choose otherwise.

translations.reason: Counterfactual conditionals require modal or possible-worlds semantics not supported in classical logic.
Simple proposition about outcome status cannot be formalized in classical logic when combined with counterfactual dependencies.
Negation of agent choice proposition cannot be formalized in classical logic when derived from counterfactual reasoning.

interpretation_notes: All claims involve counterfactual or modal elements requiring non-classical semantics. The argument structure (modus tollens) is preserved but cannot be formalized in classical logic due to the counterfactual premise.
